protections: P1: a user who saves a job with a 'Build other projects' BuildTrigger must hold Item.BUILD on every downstream project it names (absent everywhere in pinned code: no Item.BUILD check in hudson/tasks/BuildTrigger.java or the submit paths; only CLI build and set-build-result check BUILD, core/src/main/java/hudson/cli/BuildCommand.java:93, core/src/main/java/hudson/cli/SetBuildResultCommand.java:51)

P2: the pseudo 'Build after other projects are built' upstream setting must not rewrite another project's BuildTrigger unless the user holds Item.CONFIGURE on that other project (absent: core/src/main/java/hudson/model/AbstractProject.java:715-761)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a fix in Project.submit looks complete because MatrixProject has its own submit that rebuilds publishers separately
a check that reads getPublishersList() looks right but sees the old list in AbstractProject.submit, and the new list has already been saved to disk if it runs after rebuildHetero

updateByXml already checks CONFIGURE (line 570), and raw config.xml / CLI update-job reads as a power-user path that bypasses the form; the XStream unmarshal never calls BuildTrigger.DescriptorImpl.newInstance
this creates a brand-new job the caller owns, so only Job.CREATE is checked (line 217); the downstream list arrives through Items.load, not through any submit
the copied BuildTrigger was written by whoever authorised the source job; the copier only inherits existing configuration

the only project it adds is 'this', which the user may already configure; the CONFIGURE check at Job.java:969 is on this project, not on the upstream project p whose publishers are rewritten and saved

conflicts.what: the loop at AbstractProject.java:715 visits every readable project; a naive 'require CONFIGURE on p or throw' breaks every save for a user who cannot configure some unrelated project. The guard must fire only when p's trigger would actually change (the hasSame short-circuit at :757), and must not silently drop an existing link to this project on a p the user cannot configure (:727-729)

if BUILD is enforced when an existing trigger is merely re-saved, copying or re-saving a job whose stored trigger names a child the current user cannot build becomes an error. That is correct for P1, but it refuses an edit that only touches unrelated fields

moving the check into a lower layer that reads the loaded publishers (onLoad or readResolve) would also run during startup Items.load and ItemListenerImpl.onRenamed, which have no user context (BuildTrigger.java:360-377), and would break loading of stored config

fairness_risks: Startup loading of stored job configs and BuildTrigger.ItemListenerImpl.onRenamed rewrite and save triggers with no user context (core/src/main/java/hudson/tasks/BuildTrigger.java:362-376); a BUILD rule that runs on every load or save would break them

No per-build authentication exists in this version (no QueueItemAuthenticator in core), so a check at trigger time in BuildTrigger.execute (core/src/main/java/hudson/tasks/BuildTrigger.java:205-216) runs as SYSTEM and is meaningless; tests must not expect a runtime refusal

Saving a project's config while leaving an existing downstream entry untouched is legitimate; refusing to save every job whose stored trigger names a project the current editor cannot build is defensible for P1 but contradicts 'unrelated edits keep working'. Tests should pin which behaviour they expect
A user with CONFIGURE on this job but not on an upstream project must still be able to save the job when the upstream list is unchanged (AbstractProject.java:757)

design.why: Five independent fix sites with different reasons to dismiss. T1 is the advisory anchor. T3 is the MiMo-type how-trap: it is hard to place the check so that it reads the new publishers before PersistedList saves them. T4 (XML update with CONFIGURE already checked) and T6 (copy inherits authorised config) are DeepSeek-type absent routes with plausible dismissals. T7 is a different protection (CONFIGURE on a neighbouring object) with a strong 'only adds this project' dismissal. T8 can be folded in as T7's must-keep-working check. T2 (Matrix) and T5 (create-from-XML) are more routes of concepts already in the design, so including them adds little independent judgement.
